es: Reconocer en publicaciones breves el falso dilema, la generalización apresurada, el ataque personal y el sesgo, y nombrar la debilidad con una razón.

teaching.en: Flawed reasoning often hides in a fallacy, a step that sounds convincing but collapses the moment someone examines it closely.
teaching.es: El razonamiento defectuoso suele esconderse en una falacia, un paso que suena convincente pero se derrumba en cuanto alguien lo examina de cerca.
teaching.explanationEs: Fallacy se refiere a un fallo del argumento, no a un dato falso.
segments: Flawed reasoning often hides in a fallacy, a step that
sounds convincing but collapses the moment someone examines it closely.
teaching.audioText: Flawed reasoning often hides in a fallacy, a step that sounds convincing but collapses the moment someone examines it closely.

teaching.en: Either we ban phones completely or students will never concentrate: a false dilemma hides a weakness, because other options exist.
teaching.es: O prohibimos los celulares por completo o los alumnos nunca se concentrarán: un falso dilema esconde un punto débil, porque existen otras opciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Un falso dilema reduce la realidad a dos opciones.
segments: Either we ban phones completely or students will never concentrate:
a false dilemma hides a weakness, because other options exist.
teaching.audioText: Either we ban phones completely or students will never concentrate: a false dilemma hides a weakness, because other options exist.

teaching.en: Two rude tourists are an unrepresentative sample, so it would be a hasty generalisation to assume that every visitor behaves the same way.
teaching.es: Dos turistas groseros son una muestra no representativa, así que sería una generalización apresurada suponer que todos los visitantes se comportan igual.
teaching.explanationEs: Assume que + oración: no lleva preposición.
segments: Two rude tourists are an unrepresentative sample, so it would be a
hasty generalisation to assume that every visitor behaves the same way.
teaching.audioText: Two rude tourists are an unrepresentative sample, so it would be a hasty generalisation to assume that every visitor behaves the same way.

teaching.en: When a reply criticises the speaker's age instead of her argument, it is a personal attack, and the original weakness remains untouched.
teaching.es: Cuando una réplica critica la edad de la oradora en lugar de su argumento, es un ataque personal, y el punto débil original queda sin tocar.
teaching.explanationEs: El ataque personal desvía la atención del argumento hacia quien habla.
segments: When a reply criticises the speaker's age instead of her argument,
it is a personal attack, and the original weakness remains untouched.
teaching.audioText: When a reply criticises the speaker's age instead of her argument, it is a personal attack, and the original weakness remains untouched.

teaching.en: To build a straw man, a writer distorts an opponent's view and then defeats the distortion, a fallacy that rewards careless listeners.
teaching.es: Para construir un hombre de paja, un autor distorsiona la postura de un rival y luego derrota esa distorsión, una falacia que premia a los oyentes descuidados.
teaching.explanationEs: Straw man = versión deformada de lo que dijo el otro.
segments: To build a straw man, a writer distorts an opponent's view
and then defeats the distortion, a fallacy that rewards careless listeners.
teaching.audioText: To build a straw man, a writer distorts an opponent's view and then defeats the distortion, a fallacy that rewards careless listeners.

teaching.en: Survey bias appears when a writer decides to cherry-pick only the answers that support the conclusion, which produces a one-sided picture.
teaching.es: El sesgo de una encuesta aparece cuando un autor decide elegir solo las respuestas que apoyan la conclusión, lo que da una imagen parcial.
teaching.explanationEs: Bias es incontable en este sentido; one-sided se escribe con guion.
segments: Survey bias appears when a writer decides to cherry-pick only the
answers that support the conclusion, which produces a one-sided picture.
teaching.audioText: Survey bias appears when a writer decides to cherry-pick only the answers that support the conclusion, which produces a one-sided picture.

choices.text: It is a hasty generalisation: it builds a rule from very few cases.
It is a false dilemma: it offers two options when others exist.
It is a personal attack: it criticises people instead of ideas.

feedback.es: La publicación presenta dos caminos como únicos; «there is simply no other choice» es la señal de un falso dilema.

hint.es: Fíjate en la estructura either … or y en la frase que niega cualquier otra opción.

origin.text: Either we ban every phone in school or our results will keep falling. There is simply no other choice, and pretending otherwise only wastes everyone's time.

prompt.es: Completa: «Decir que todos los turistas son groseros es una generalización apresurada.»

feedback.es: Hasty generalisation es el nombre de la falacia que convierte dos casos en una regla general.

hint.es: Sustantivo: regla general sacada de pocos casos.

origin.text: Two rude tourists tell us very little about millions of visitors. To conclude that every tourist is rude is a hasty ___ drawn from an unrepresentative sample.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Su réplica fue un ataque personal que ignoró por completo mi argumento.»

answer.text: Her reply was a personal attack that ignored my argument completely

feedback.es: Personal attack + that ignored…: la relativa explica por qué el ataque no resuelve nada: el argumento ni se examina.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto Her reply; completely va al final.

prompt.es: ¿Qué debilidad tiene la encuesta del texto?

choices.text: The survey is too old to describe what the town thinks today.
The percentage is misleading, because the pool's cost is never mentioned.
Only people already using the pool were asked, so the sample cannot speak for the town.
The question was worded so that members could only answer yes.

feedback.es: Solo se preguntó a quienes salían de la piscina un sábado: una muestra no representativa que no puede hablar en nombre de toda la ciudad.

origin.text: Our club's survey shows that 95 per cent of members love the new pool. We asked only the people leaving the pool on Saturday morning, but the result is clear: the whole town is delighted.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hizo Sara en el debate.

choices.text: She exposed the lack of evidence behind his proposal.
She distorted his proposal and then defeated the distorted version.
She offered two extreme options and ignored every other one.
She attacked his background instead of examining his proposal.

feedback.es: Sara desvió la atención hacia la persona de Carlos; por eso su punto débil real, la falta de pruebas, no llegó a discutirse.

origin.audio: Carlos argued for longer school days. His opponent, Sara, did not answer him. Instead she said that a man who never teaches could hardly understand pupils. Everyone cheered, but notice what happened: she attacked the speaker, not the argument. His proposal was never discussed, and its real weakness, a lack of evidence, was never exposed.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada enunciado con la debilidad que muestra.

pairs: Either we ban phones or students fail.
Two rude drivers, so everyone here drives badly.
You are too young to judge this.
She quoted only the figures that helped her.

feedback.es: Cada enunciado ejemplifica una debilidad distinta: dos opciones, pocos casos, ataque a la persona y datos escogidos.

pairs: Either we ban phones or students fail.
Two rude drivers, so everyone here drives badly.
You are too young to judge this.
She quoted only the figures that helped her.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige lo que la locutora da a entender sobre el proyecto del estacionamiento.

choices.text: It may be a good idea, even though its defence is weak.
It is a bad idea, because the mayor defends it so badly.
The survey proves that the car park will not help any shop.
The shop owner's interest means that her survey is useless.

feedback.es: La locutora admite que el estacionamiento «may well help», pero critica el argumento que lo defiende: no descalifica el proyecto, solo su defensa.

origin.audio: A local mayor posted a message online. Either the town builds a new car park, he wrote, or shops will close one by one. When a shop owner replied that an earlier survey had suggested other options, the mayor answered that she was hardly a neutral voice, since her own shop was beside the market. Notice what is missing: he never discussed her survey, and he offered no figures of his own. His case rests on two weak steps: a choice between only two futures, and the rejection of the person who questions it. The car park may well help. But the argument in its favour is a poor one.

prompt.es: ¿Qué debilidad tiene la respuesta del bloguero?

choices.text: It assumes that every student dislikes homework on any topic.
It distorts her proposal and then attacks the distorted version.
It draws a general rule from two or three students' behaviour.
It criticises the teacher's character instead of her suggestion.

feedback.es: El bloguero convierte «un poco de elección» en «hacer lo que quieran» y rebate esa versión deformada: es un hombre de paja, no un ataque personal.

origin.text: Teacher: We should give students a little choice about their homework topics. Blogger: So the teacher wants students to do whatever they like and never work hard. Schools cannot run on doing nothing, and a school that trusts its pupils to choose will soon lose control, so her idea must be rejected.

prompt.es: Completa: «El autor está eligiendo solo las pruebas que encajan con su tesis.»

feedback.es: Cherry-picking describe elegir solo los datos favorables y dejar fuera el resto: el informe cita tres estudios a favor e ignora los otros diez.

origin.text: The report mentions the three studies that support the plan and ignores the other ten. The writer is clearly cherry-___ the evidence to suit his case.

prompt.es: Nombra la debilidad de esta publicación y da una razón con because.

answer.text: This is a hasty generalisation, because it draws a general rule about every app from the experience of one person.
accepted: This is a hasty generalisation, because it draws a general rule about every app from the experience of one person.
It is a hasty generalisation, since it builds a general rule about all apps from just one person's experience.
The post is a hasty generalization because one case cannot prove anything about every app.

feedback.es: Se nombra la falacia (hasty generalisation) y se justifica con because: un solo caso no permite hablar de todas las apps.

origin.text: Publicación: «Mi primo probó esa app y no le funcionó, así que ninguna app sirve para aprender idiomas.» Nombra la debilidad y explica por qué.

prompt.es: ¿Qué opina el autor del aplauso del público?

choices.text: It proves the minister answered his critics in a convincing way.
It was unfair, because the audience had not seen the figures.
It shows enthusiasm more than it proves that the argument was sound.
It was deserved, even though the minister skipped the figures.

feedback.es: El autor dice que el aplauso revela más entusiasmo que calidad del argumento: el ministro ni siquiera mencionó las cifras de sus rivales.

origin.text: In his closing speech the minister claimed that critics of the plan were friends of chaos. He did not mention the figures his opponents had produced. The audience cheered loudly, which says more about its enthusiasm than about the quality of the argument, and the newspapers then repeated the slogan without checking it.

prompt.es: Completa: «La muestra no es representativa de toda la ciudad.»

feedback.es: Una muestra elegida en una sola calle es unrepresentative: no refleja la variedad de la ciudad.

origin.text: A survey of twenty people, all chosen from one street, cannot speak for the whole town. The sample is ___.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La falacia consiste en dar por sentado que solo existen dos opciones.»

answer.text: The fallacy lies in assuming that only two options exist

feedback.es: Lies in + gerundio indica dónde está el fallo: en dar por sentado algo que no se ha demostrado.
